# Brain Audit

Score the second brain, store the score, propose two builds. Then stop.

The point is the **trend**, not any single run. A score that only exists once is
the failure this skill was built to fix: `~/SecondBrain/audits/` held exactly one
report for 45 days before this skill existed.

## Step 1 — measure

```bash
bash ~/.claude/skills/brain-audit/measure.sh
```

Facts only, ~7 seconds. **Never estimate a number this script reports.** If a
value reads `MISSING` or `none`, that is a finding, not an error to work around.

## Step 2 — score the four C's, 25 points each

Anchor every score to a measured number so two runs a month apart are comparable.

| C | What it measures | 25 pts | 13 pts | 0 pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Context** | Evergreen facts on disk | `USER.md` + `MEMORY.md` under cap, 35+ Tier A memories, `Knowledge/` touched <14d | one file over cap, or `Knowledge/` 14–45d stale | a memory file MISSING, or `Knowledge/` >45d stale |
| **Connections** | Live data arriving | `meeting_sync` <7d, `portfolio_json` <14d, `ledger` <30d | one source 2× its window | two or more sources silent |
| **Capabilities** | Skills that get used | audit-driven builds shipped since last run | skills exist, none exercised | skills installed and never run |
| **Cadence** | What keeps it alive | all launchd jobs `exit=0` **and** `Notes/` <21d | jobs green, `Notes/` 21–45d | `Notes/` >45d, or any job non-zero |

Cadence is scored hardest on `Notes/`, not on the jobs. Every job being green while
synthesis is frozen is the exact failure this system keeps repeating.

## Step 3 — run the three tests

Answer each with evidence from Step 1, and mark pass / warn / fail.

1. **Teammate test.** A teammate asks a question. Would the system answer it faster
   than Eric from memory, with sources? Evidence: is the answer actually filed, or
   still only in his head?
2. **Context-switch test.** Can the work be done from one surface? Evidence: command
   centre and dashboard freshness.
3. **Head-emptying test.** Has a decision been captured, or is it being re-litigated?
   Evidence: open items in `MEMORY.md` "Pending Decisions" with no note behind them.

These shape the narrative. They do not move the number.

## Step 4 — write the report

`~/SecondBrain/audits/brain-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, frontmatter `type: resource`.

Sections: score table (four C's + total) → the three tests → what would make the
agent wrong-answer him today → the two proposed builds.

Then append one row to `~/SecondBrain/audits/_trend.md` (create with a header if
absent):

You are close. You already have about 3 of the 5 ideas. Two pieces are missing.

**What I did:** I read the PDF. I compared its 5 ideas to your setup.

## Score by idea

| # | Idea in the doc | You have | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Research first | The `last30days` skill is installed. You did video gap reviews on 9/1 and 9/7. | ✅ Have it |
| 2 | Learn from 4 open projects | **Karpathy wiki** = your memory compiler (525 articles plus `index.md`). **qmd** (search by meaning) = `memsearch`. **Graphify** = installed. **gbrain** (cite sources, clean itself) = partly there, through `improve-system` and `brain-audit`. | 🟡 Mostly |
| 3 | Plain code finds the answer, and the model is called once at the end | Missing. `memsearch` gives back the top chunks, but no code walks the ladder: keywords → score the index → open 1 file → read 1 section. Saving a memory uses the `memory-write` skill, so it needs the model. | ❌ Gap |
| 4 | A small index of everything | Strong. You have the `MEMORY.md` indexes, the `DEV/CLAUDE.md` router, and the knowledge `index.md`. `memory-write` adds the index line each time it saves. | ✅ Have it |
| 5 | Prove it works | Missing. No test compares tokens and time against a fresh default session. `brain-audit` scores the brain's health, not what a lookup costs. | ❌ Gap |

**One more thing:** `brain-audit` ran only once, on 2026-09-07 (score 67). That was 46 days ago. Your own note says manual steps stop within 6 weeks unless a timer runs them. That has happened here too.

## Pick one

1. **Test first (I'd go with this one).** Pick 5 real questions from your work. Answer each one twice: once in a fresh default session, once through `memsearch`. Measure tokens, time, and whether the answer is right. Cost: about 30 minutes. If your current setup already wins, you build nothing.
2. **Build now.** Write `recall.py`. It runs the plain-code ladder over your existing indexes. Also write a `remember` command that saves a memory and its index line with no model call. Cost: about 2 hours.

I'd go with option 1. Your doc says the gain shows up on hard questions (facts deep inside files, answers that need more than one file). The test shows if you have that problem before you spend the 2 hours.

**Not checked:** I did not read the 9/1 and 9/7 video reviews in full. I did not run `memsearch` to see how good its results are.

name: headless-claude-tool-deny-gap
description: "`claude -p --disallowedTools Bash` still runs shell commands through context-mode MCP tools — a headless smoke test is not read-only"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9823c1f0-89f5-4638-9223-c6892607ac2b
  modified: 2026-09-13T06:16:42.437Z
---

`claude -p "..." --disallowedTools Bash` does **not** stop shell execution. The
context-mode plugin's MCP tools (`ctx_execute`, `ctx_batch_execute`,
`ctx_execute_file`) run shell commands and are not covered by denying `Bash`.
Seen 2026-09-12: a headless "audit my AI OS" smoke test with Bash denied still
ran `aios-metrics.py` through the MCP shell.

**Why:** a smoke test believed to be read-only can run, and in principle write,
anything the MCP shell can.

**How to apply:** for a truly read-only headless run, also deny the
`mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__*` tools (or disable the plugin). Then
check for side effects afterwards (git status, memory dirs). Never report a headless
run as "no side effects possible" on the Bash deny alone.

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run opens a Terminal window. Eric set profile "Clear Dark" to "Close if the shell exited cleanly" (10-23, in Terminal Settings; a `defaults import` did not reach the running Terminal), so the window closes when the copy ends (tested). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. folder is 0 KB on disk — all cloud placeholders). `stat()` and `os.walk` are fine: five Drive
folders, 76k files, 10 seconds by name+size.

One folder hangs even on listing: `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/02_Raw_Tagging`
(thousands of face images). Skip it in any Drive walk.

**DEFAULT (Eric, 2026-10-17): read or copy any Drive file through the gws API, never through the
mount.** The mount is for `ls`/`stat` only. 2026-10-17 a `cp` of a 24 MB workbook sat at 0 bytes, twice,
even after Eric quit and reopened Google Drive; the API pulled it in seconds:
- Find the id: `gws drive files list --params '{"q":"name contains '\''<name>'\'' and trashed=false","fields":"files(id,name,size,parents)"}'`

- Same name can exist twice (a copy in `Send/`); pick by `parents`.

**How to apply:**
- Compare Drive copies by `(basename, size)`, never by content. `~/DEV/_INBOX/tools/drain_diff.py --names-only`.
- Move or rename Drive folders with the Drive MCP (`update_file` with `parentId`) — server-side, instant,

# Connection: VALD ForceDecks CMJ Data Across Baylor Projects

## The Connection

The same underlying data source - VALD ForceDecks countermovement jump (CMJ) force-plate testing - shows up in two otherwise unrelated Baylor Athletics efforts. On 2026-04-14, a 67-session VALD ForceDecks CMJ export was turned into individual return-to-competition reports for [[concepts/skylar-zinnecker-cmj-rtc-reports]]. On 2026-06-10, a much larger CMJ backfill (2,531 tests, 103,769 metric rows) for the [[concepts/keystone-os-tezino-project]] used the same VALD ForceDecks data source at teamscale, including the mRSI (reactive strength index) metric.

## Key Insight

The two projects represent opposite ends of the same data pipeline's use cases: one is a single-athlete, clinically-framed report generated from a CSV export for a specific decision (RTC clearance), while the other is a team-wide, database-backed narrative dataset used to track readiness trends over a training cycle. Both rely on the same VALD metrics vocabulary - mRSI appears as a key indicator in both the Zinnecker baseline/current comparison context and the Tezino summer-2025 readiness decline. This suggests VALD ForceDecks/CMJ data (and metrics like mRSI, asymmetry, and jump-height/stiffness) form a shared vocabulary across Baylor's individual-athlete and team-level sports-science tooling, and that improvements built for one use case (e.g., baseline-redefinition logic, or automated injury/trend annotation) may be portable to the other.

## Evidence

- 2026-04-14 (17:27): "Processed VALD ForceDecks export (`CMJ-test-export-04_14_2026.csv`, 67 sessions, Aug 2023-Apr 2026)" into per-athlete RTC reports, with baseline redefined to the last 4 pre-injury sessions.
- 2026-06-10: Summer 2025 CMJ backfill pulled "2,531 tests / 103,769 metric rows" team-wide, with Tezino's mRSI dropping from 0.577 (Apr) to 0.407 (Jul 2025) - the same mRSI metric used in individual CMJ analysis.

## Related Concepts

- [[concepts/skylar-zinnecker-cmj-rtc-reports]]
- [[concepts/keystone-os-tezino-project]]

#!/bin/bash
# Brain test: same 5 questions, two arms, same model.
#   A = fresh default session in ~/DEV (finds the answer however it likes)
#   B = memsearch top-5 (plain code) -> one model call, no tools, evidence attached
OUT="$(dirname "$0")/out"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
cd ~/DEV || exit 1

QS=(
"What was the total score of my first brain audit, and what were the four sub-scores?"
"Why did the cloud-push launchd job fail to copy to Google Drive, and how was it fixed?"
"How should I copy a 24 MB file off the Google Drive mount, and which folder should every Drive walk skip?"
"How many CMJ tests and metric rows were in the summer 2025 CMJ backfill?"
"In the AIOS video gap analysis, what four things were missing, and which two builds did the first brain audit propose?"
)

for i in "${!QS[@]}"; do
  n=$((i+1)); q="${QS[$i]}"
  echo "== Q$n"

  # Arm A: default session
  s=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')
  claude -p "$q Answer in 3 sentences or fewer." --model sonnet --output-format json \
    --permission-mode bypassPermissions --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1 \
    > "$OUT/A$n.json" 2> "$OUT/A$n.err"
  e=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')
  echo "$s $e" > "$OUT/A$n.wall"

  # Arm B: memsearch, then one tool-less model call
  s=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')
  memsearch search "$q" --top-k 5 > "$OUT/B$n.evidence" 2>&1
  m=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')
  claude -p "Answer the question using ONLY the evidence below, in 3 sentences or fewer. If the evidence does not answer it, say NOT FOUND.

Question: $q

Evidence:
$(cat "$OUT/B$n.evidence")" --model sonnet --output-format json --tools "" --strict-mcp-config \
    --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1 \
    > "$OUT/B$n.json" 2> "$OUT/B$n.err"
  e=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())')
  echo "$s $m $e" > "$OUT/B$n.wall"
done
echo DONE

import json, pathlib, sys

out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
rows = []
for n in range(1, 6):
    for arm in "AB":
        try:
            j = json.loads((out / f"{arm}{n}.json").read_text())
        except Exception as ex:
            print(f"Q{n} {arm}: no JSON ({ex})"); continue
        u = j.get("usage", {})
        tok = sum(u.get(k, 0) for k in ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens",
                                       "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        w = [float(x) for x in (out / f"{arm}{n}.wall").read_text().split()]
        wall = w[-1] - w[0]
        ms = (w[1] - w[0]) if arm == "B" else None
        rows.append((n, arm, tok, j.get("total_cost_usd", 0), wall, ms, j.get("num_turns"),
                     (j.get("result") or "").replace("\n", " ")))

print("| Q | Arm | Tokens | Cost $ | Wall s | memsearch s | Turns |")
print("|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
for n, arm, tok, cost, wall, ms, turns, _ in rows:
    print(f"| {n} | {arm} | {tok:,} | {cost:.3f} | {wall:.1f} | {'' if ms is None else f'{ms:.1f}'} | {turns} |")
for arm in "AB":
    r = [x for x in rows if x[1] == arm]
    if r:
        print(f"TOTAL {arm}: tokens {sum(x[2] for x in r):,}  cost ${sum(x[3] for x in r):.3f}  wall {sum(x[4] for x in r):.0f}s")
print()
for n, arm, *_, ans in rows:
    print(f"Q{n} {arm}: {ans}\n")

- **B** = `memsearch` finds 5 pieces of text, then the model answers from only those pieces.

## What this means

1. **Your indexes work.** Questions 1 to 3 are in your memory index. Session A read the index, opened 1 file, and got each one right in under a minute. Your doc said this would happen.
2. **`memsearch` is the weak part.** Each search took 53 to 166 seconds. It gave back text that was cut off before the answer.
3. **Question 4 is the one place B won.** The fact was deep in an old note. B was right, twice as fast, and used about 1/5 of the tokens.
4. **Both failed question 5.** Session A started a background search and lost its own answer. B's text was cut off again.

1. **Build `recall.py` (I'd go with this one).** It is plain code that does what session A did: read the index → open 1 file → read 1 section. It uses `memsearch` only when the index has no match. Then I run this same test again to compare. About 2 hours.
2. **Fix `memsearch` speed first.** Searches that take 1 to 3 minutes are a problem on their own. But a faster search still gives back cut-off text, so this fixes only half of the problem.
